h1: The 7 Best Cordless Vacuums for Hardwood Floors of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 7 cordless stick vacuums for hardwood homes, sorted by runtime, power and price tier, with picks for every budget.
summary: Our top pick for a hardwood home is the Levoit Cordless Vacuum with a 60 minute runtime on its spec sheet. The Shark PowerPro Flex Reveal Plus is the brand-name choice at a lower price tier. The mohomo is the longest-running option at 70 minutes, and the TechRise is the cheapest way into a 550W cordless stick.
intro: The classic mistake with a cordless vacuum on hardwood is buying on suction wattage alone. Hardwood needs a head that picks up dust without scattering it, and a battery that lasts through a whole floor, so runtime and head design matter more than a big number on the box.

We reviewed seven cordless vacuums from the listings and spec sheets and ranked them on runtime, stated power, and price tier. Because the data covers runtime and wattage but little about brush design, we flag where you should check the listing before buying.

products.name: Levoit Cordless Vacuum
products.verdict: A 60 minute runtime in a smaller footprint makes it the most practical whole-home pick.
products.description:
The Levoit Cordless Vacuum lists a 60 minute runtime, which is enough to cover a full hardwood floor plan without a mid-job recharge. It sits in the $200-500 bracket, the priciest tier in this ranking.

It earns the top spot over the Shark PowerPro Flex Reveal Plus by adding ten minutes of listed runtime and a smaller footprint, but you pay for that in a higher price bracket than almost everything below it.

Buy it if you have a compact home and want to clean in one pass. The catch is that the data we have says nothing about brush type, so confirm a soft or hard-floor head on the listing.
products.idealFor: Small homes that want one-pass cleaning.

products.name: Shark PowerPro Flex Reveal Plus Cordless Vacuum
products.verdict: A 50 minute runtime from a familiar vacuum brand at a mid price.
products.description:
The Shark PowerPro Flex Reveal Plus lists 50 minutes of runtime and falls in the $100-200 bracket. That combination makes it the easiest recommendation for buyers who want a known name.

It ranks below the Levoit because it gives up ten minutes of runtime, but it costs less than the top pick. Against the mohomo it trades 20 minutes of runtime for a more established brand.

Choose it for a mid-size home where 50 minutes is plenty. The caveat is that the listing data does not give a wattage figure, so compare suction claims on the page itself.
products.idealFor: Buyers who prefer a familiar brand.
products.skipIf: You need over an hour of runtime.

products.name: mohomo Cordless Vacuum Cleaner
products.verdict: The 70 minute battery is the longest of the group.
products.description:
The mohomo lists 70 minutes of runtime and 650W, the highest figures on both counts in this ranking, at a $100-200 price.

It sits third because the brand is less established than Levoit or Shark, even though its numbers are better on paper. Against the TechRise it adds ten minutes and 100W for a higher price bracket.

It suits large homes with a lot of floor to cover. The caveat is that wattage and runtime are manufacturer claims, so check owner feedback for how the battery holds up.
products.idealFor: Large homes with lots of floor.
products.skipIf: Brand reputation matters most to you.

products.name: Levoit Cordless Vacuum Cleaner
products.verdict: A 50 minute runtime from Levoit without the top price tier.
products.description:
This Levoit lists 50 minutes of runtime and sits in the $100-200 bracket, cheaper than the other Levoit in this guide.

It ranks fourth because it matches the Shark on runtime but offers fewer listed extras. Against the Levoit above it, you lose ten minutes and gain a lower price tier.

It fits apartments and mid-size homes. The caveat is the sparse spec sheet, so read the listing for head and filter details.

products.name: TechRise Cordless Vacuum Cleaner
products.verdict: The cheapest entry here, with 60 minutes and 550W listed.
products.description:
The TechRise is in the $50-100 tier, the lowest in this ranking, yet lists 60 minutes of runtime and 550W.

It ranks fifth because the brand is unproven, though the numbers rival pricier picks. Against the iXlion it adds five minutes of runtime and a stated wattage.

Pick it if budget decides. The risk is that low-cost stick vacuums can vary on build quality, so check owner feedback.
products.skipIf: You want a brand with long support history.

products.name: iXlion Cordless Vacuum Cleaner for Home
products.verdict: A 55 minute runtime in the $50-100 tier.
products.description:
The iXlion lists 55 minutes of runtime in the $50-100 price tier.

It ranks sixth because the TechRise offers more runtime and a wattage figure at the same tier. It is a reasonable alternative if the TechRise is unavailable.

It suits small homes and secondary floors. The listing data is thin, so verify the head and bin details.
products.skipIf: You want a detailed spec sheet.

products.name: Shark Pet Cordless Stick Vacuum
products.verdict: A Shark stick with 40 minutes, best for small spaces.
products.description:
The Shark Pet Cordless Stick Vacuum lists 40 minutes of runtime in the $100-200 tier.

It lands last because its runtime is the shortest here and it costs more than the budget picks. The Shark name is its main appeal.

Choose it for small hardwood areas and quick cleanups. For a whole house, a longer-running pick is smarter.
products.skipIf: You clean a whole house in one go.

whatMatters.detail: Runtime is how many minutes the battery lasts on its normal setting. On a hardwood floor plan of several rooms, 50 minutes or more avoids a mid-clean recharge. Look for the minutes figure in the title or bullets, and note whether it refers to the lowest power mode.

The head is what touches the floor. A soft roller picks up fine dust without scattering it, while a stiff bristle brush can scuff or flick debris on hard surfaces. The listing should name the head, so look for words like soft roller or hard floor mode.

Wattage is a rough indicator of motor draw, not a measure of cleaning. Higher numbers like 650W suggest more suction but also drain the battery faster. Compare wattage only between similar models, and read it as a ceiling rather than a guarantee.

A small bin forces frequent stops, which cuts into the battery you paid for. Check the bin capacity and whether it empties without touching dust. This detail is missing on many listings, so check the product images.

Batteries age, and filters and brush rolls wear out. A known brand usually means replacement parts are easy to find years later. Search the listing for replacement battery and filter availability before you buy.

faq.q: Are cordless vacuums safe for hardwood floors?
faq.a: Generally yes if the head has soft bristles or a soft roller. Check the listing for a hard floor mode or soft head before buying.

faq.q: What is the most common mistake buyers make?
faq.a: Buying on wattage alone. A big number does little if the head scatters debris or the battery dies after 20 minutes.

faq.q: Is the Levoit worth more than the Shark?
faq.a: It adds ten minutes of listed runtime and a smaller footprint, but costs more. If 50 minutes is enough, the Shark saves money.

faq.q: How do I set up a cordless vacuum?
faq.a: Charge the battery fully before first use, assemble the wand and head, and mount the dock on a wall near an outlet if included.
Empty the bin after each use, clean or replace the filter on the schedule in the manual, and clear hair from the roller.

faq.q: Can a cordless vacuum replace a plug-in model?
faq.a: For most hardwood homes, yes, if the runtime covers your floor plan. Very large homes may still benefit from a second battery or a corded unit.

finalTake: The Levoit Cordless Vacuum is our top pick for its 60 minute runtime and compact build. The Shark PowerPro Flex Reveal Plus is the safe brand choice, and the mohomo is the endurance pick. Budget buyers can start with the TechRise. Before you buy any of them, confirm the head type on the listing.
